transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-10-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Onyx Head of ML), David Li (Onyx Platform), Hector Alvarez (Onyx CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: medium-quality auto-summary present; see 'summary' field above

Topics: model routing, prefix/KV prefetch, batching economics, per-route cost allocation

[00:00] Janelle: ok everyone thanks for joining from Redwood, appreciate you squeezing this in. rough plan: 45 minute walkthrough of our Optimize playbook in the console, then 15 for Q&A and pilot logistics. Mateo will lead the technical part.
[00:22] Mateo: hey all, hi Priya, David, Hector. quick confirm — you sent the session heatmap and a small sample of requests earlier today? i have those loaded into the sandbox but if there's more please drop it in the shared folder.
[00:38] Priya: yes i uploaded anonymized traces, maybe 72 hours, but there's some heavy tail at peak 11am PT. want us to highlight the user prompt lengths — average 190 tokens but a long tail to 1600.
[00:55] David: also, our usage pattern has a lot of short assistant-turns interleaved with a few long generation bursts — that's why we care about prefetch and session affinity.
[01:12] Mateo: perfect. quick overview — Optimize recommends three levers: routing (latency vs cost tiers), batching (throughput concurrency), and KV/prefix caching (prefetching likely prefixes). coupling those gets you big unit-cost wins without sacrificing SLO.
[01:35] Hector: can you explain routing tiers? we currently host on GCP with mixed GPUs; worried about failing over to a slower quantized model.
[01:50] Mateo: yes — routing policy can be per-route: e.g. 'primary-low-latency' (non-quantized, reserved capacity), 'economy' (quantized variants or higher-batch nodes), and 'fallback' (cross-region or lower-cost). we do automatic fallback but you control allowed feature set — e.g. disable tool-calls on economy.
[02:18] Speaker 1: sorry interject — is there a way to pin a subset of customers to dedicated pool?
[02:25] Janelle: yeah we support tenant pinning; Dedicated capacity can be reserved and then policy routes specific API keys there.
[02:38] Priya: what about latency budgets — our SLO is p95 < 200ms on short prompts and < 1s on long ones.
[02:48] Mateo: based on your traces, short prompts will hit ~120ms on primary lanes with continuous batching tuned to 64 token context. long bursts depend on concurrency; with prefix cache prefetching we reduce token compute for repeated system prefixes by ~30-60% in our sims.
[03:12] David: how do you measure that in the console? is there a per-route cost breakdown?
[03:19] Mateo: yes — Optimize console shows token-level unit cost, prefix cache hit rate, batching latency curve, and per-route spend attribution. we also show simulated savings if you enable prefetch windows or increase concurrency limits.
[03:38] Priya: i saw the dashboard screenshot in the doc but curious about the simulation fidelity — how close are sim numbers to real runs?
[03:48] Mateo: depends on fidelity of traces. with real session traces we tend to be within 5-12% of actual spend; synthetic traces can be off more. that's why we recommended the 2-week pilot with real traffic and a controlled reserved capacity lane.
[04:08] Janelle: quick note on security — Onyx asked earlier about KMS and audit logs: our private deployment integrates KMS, HSM options, and we surface audit logs in the Console; SOC2 report + ISO request handled via our security package.
[04:23] Hector: good. one more question — how will prefix cache interact with user-specific context? we have per-customer system messages.
[04:35] Mateo: prefix cache works best when prefixes are shared across requests — system prompts or helper prompts that repeat. for per-customer system prompts we can namespace the cache by tenant but that reduces hit rate. you can also prefetch only shared prefixes and keep tenant-specific tokens computed.
[04:58] Priya: can you demo a prefetch policy? like prefetch top 5 prefixes per session?
[05:05] Mateo: sure turning to the console — (shared deck link: https://redwood.in/optimize-deck) — here in the Optimize Playbook, we have a 'prefetch policy' panel. you choose window size (e.g., lookahead 3 tokens, or top-k prefixes), TTL, and cost threshold. i'll run a live sim with your traces.
[05:34] [screen share noise, brief pause]
[05:45] Mateo: running simulation... ok initial baseline: no prefetch, primary routing only: projected monthly token compute $18.3k (normalized). enabling prefix prefetch top-k=5 with TTL=30s reduces compute by 21% in simulation to ~$14.4k. adding route balancing to allow 15% of traffic to 'economy' quantized nodes reduces further to ~$11.1k but increases p95 for long turns by ~120ms.
[06:30] David: that's compelling. what's the tradeoff with concurrency — do we need more concurrency to realize batching wins?
[06:38] Mateo: yes batching is a function of concurrency and arrival pattern. If you increase concurrency cap from 8->24 per model instance, average batch size goes up, lowering per-token cost, but latency tail may worsen if requests are waiting. we simulate concurrency sensitivity — for your traces optimal concurrency seemed around 16 for peak periods.
[07:02] Priya: can you show the per-route SLA impact table?
[07:07] Mateo: pulling it up — (table in console) shows routes: primary (p95 120ms), economy(p95 260ms), fallback cross-region(p95 420ms). we annotate expected cost per 1M tokens: primary $7.1k, economy $3.8k, fallback $1.9k in our estimates. these are normalized and depend on exact instance types.
[07:36] Hector: are those numbers per 1M tokens or per-month at our projected volume?
[07:41] Mateo: per 1M tokens normalized. we'll attach the cost spreadsheet with instance assumptions so you can map to your forecast.
[07:50] Speaker 2: small transcription glitch — "prefetch" was transcribed as "pre-fish" earlier in notes, just flagging.
[07:56] Janelle: noted, i see it in the doc, we'll clean it up. but the raw transcript will include that mis-transcribe.
[08:05] Priya: okay can we talk about pilot shape — do you recommend dedicated capacity for first 2 weeks?
[08:13] Mateo: yes — recommended pilot: reserve a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs depending on model) for primary lane for baseline run, enable prefetch policy and simulated routing with 10-20% traffic to economy to compare. we'll run daily cost/latency snapshots and adjust TTL/top-k.
[08:36] David: who runs the benchmark? Redwood or Onyx?
[08:40] Janelle: we'll run it jointly — Mateo will set up the simulation and we request traces; Onyx provides the traces and synthetic load generator if you want isolated bursts.
[08:51] Priya: timeline — we need results before our Nov 14 roadmap review.
[08:57] Mateo: feasible — pilot start Nov 1, two week run, report Nov 15. that lines up with your roadmap.
[09:07] Hector: what about compliance during pilot — we'll need audit logs and SSO configured.
[09:13] Janelle: yes we'll provision a private project for the pilot with SAML SSO (Okta), KMS enabled, and access controls. security engineer will share a checklist.
[09:28] [longer section of Q&A — snippets]
[09:30] Priya: if we enable prefix cache, how do we handle invalidation when system prompt changes?
[09:38] Mateo: TTL-based invalidation; also we support pinned cache keys you can flush via API on rollouts.
[09:45] David: what's the ops burden for maintaining prefetch rules?
[09:49] Mateo: usually small — Optimize console provides recommendations and suggested rules (auto-suggest) and we can export them as IaC to your repo.
[10:01] Priya: any differences for on-prem vs VPC private deploy?
[10:08] Mateo: same features; on-prem means you'll host runtime and we ship the control plane (or you can run control plane in VPC). KV cache is local to runtime clusters so hit rates are even better on-prem.
[10:20] [pause]
[10:25] Janelle: ok wrapping — quick recap from my side.
[10:28] Janelle: agreed pilot Nov 1 start, Onyx to send more traces by Oct 31, Redwood to share cost model & pilot runbook by Oct 29, security checklist to follow.
[10:40] Priya: confirmed. also want a quick demo for product teams — can we record a 20m technical demo for internal docs?
[10:46] Janelle: yes will do; we'll send recording and a short 20m excerpt targeted at product.
[10:53] Hector: thanks everyone. one last question — what if we hit capacity limits during pilot and need to burst?
[10:58] Mateo: we support burst capacity on Dedicated with autoscale; we can provision burst lanes that tap into spare pool. there'll be cost surcharge but we can model that in the spreadsheet.
[11:10] [closing]
[11:12] Janelle: thanks all — action items and next steps in calendar invite. we'll follow up in chat with the deck link and files.
[11:20] Mateo: thanks, bye.

End Transcript
